subject: Usage tier carveouts and stepdown discount conditions
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: RFP pricing clarifications — tier carveouts and stepdown questions

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the initial commercial attachment in the RFP. A couple of points we need clarified for the pricing section before we loop in legal:

1) Stepdown discounts: your response shows a "stepdown" at the 2M token band (10% -> 5%) — can you confirm whether the stepdown is volume-aggregated (monthly) or measured on committed baseline only? Acme requires clarity on whether we retain the higher discount on consumption above the band during the month or if the lower step applies retroactively.

2) Carveouts: we have three traffic types (inference generation, embeddings, and fine-tune store). Which of these are eligible for the committed bucket by default vs carved out as billable at list? We need a simple table we can hand to procurement.

3) Overage path and monthly true-up cadence: the RFP asks for both monthly true-up and 30-day overage invoicing options — can you outline what the preferred commercial practice is for Redwood and whether a quarterly true-up is supported for enterprise accounts?

4) Price parity on embeddings: are embeddings priced differently (per-embedding-unit) or do you map to token-equivalent pricing? If the former, what is the per-1k-embedding-unit list price and the overage price after commit?

Attached is the excerpt from Section C that lists our ask. If you can provide a short matrix (+1 page summary) we can incorporate into the procurement scorecard.

Would also like to set a quick 30-min sync tomorrow to confirm. Proposed slot: Wed 08/12 10:30 PT.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Health
Acme Health — Strategic Sourcing
Attachment: Acme_RFP_section_C_pricing.pdf

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP pricing clarifications — tier carveouts and stepdown questions

Samantha —

Thanks for the clear ask and the RFP excerpt — appreciate the specificity. Below are concise answers and an attached matrix (redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx) that maps the commercial mechanics you requested.

1) Stepdown behavior: Stepdowns are applied on a "month-of" aggregated consumption basis. The discount tier that applies is determined by the total monthly usage across billable token classes that are in-scope of the committed bucket. If the month crosses a higher band, the higher discount applies to the portion of volume within that band (i.e., not retroactive to earlier usage). We can add a one-line alternative to apply retroactive step if Acme prefers that negotiation path (commonly used for multi-year locked deals).

2) Carveouts: By default Redwood's committed bucket includes generation and embeddings for application inference traffic. Fine-tune store (persistent model store) and third-party tooling calls are carved out as billable at list by default. See attached matrix: column A lists traffic type, column B = included in commit (Y/N), column C = default overage metric. We are open to moving embeddings to a separate commitment band if you prefer distinct economics.

3) True-up cadence / Overage: Standard practice for enterprise is monthly true-up with invoiced overages on the following monthly invoice. Quarterly true-up is supported for committed customers and is a common concession for larger annual commitments; this would require a 60–90 day billing lead notice for forecasting. We can propose quarterly true-up in the term sheet and map invoicing cadence accordingly.

4) Embeddings pricing: We price embeddings on a per-1k-embedding-unit basis for clarity in analytics workflows. List price: $40 / 1k embedding-units. Committed overage price: $28 / 1k embedding-units (post-commit discount ladder). If you prefer a token-equivalent approach we can provide a mapping table, but embedding units are more stable for usage forecasting.

Negotiation levers we recommend (short):
- One-time onboarding credit to offset piloting costs
- Capped overage liability for first 3 months post-go-live
- Option for quarterly true-up in exchange for a 6–9% volume commit uplift

I've attached the pricing matrix and a short one-pager summary. If this looks good, I can have legal/finance convert the bullets into a draft commercial term sheet for redlines.

I can take the proposed slot tomorrow 10:30 PT; I booked it tentatively — meeting invite follows.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RFP pricing clarifications — tier carveouts and stepdown questions

Looping in a few commercial plays we should offer in the term sheet. Quick notes for the draft: 

- Add a one-time onboarding credit (up to $25k) tied to a 12-month commit to de-risk pilot conversion.
- Provide a 90-day capped overage liability equal to 15% of committed spend for the first quarter post-go-live; after that, standard overage terms apply.
- Separate embeddings into an optional additive commitment band (Emb-Band) so Acme can choose to put embeddings into either commit or pay-as-you-go.
- Offer a "retroactive step" clause as trade for a 5% increase in committed volume (if they want retroactive higher-tier pricing applied to the full month).

I'll prepare a compact commercial-term-sheet-draft.pdf for legal/finance to review; attaching draft for reference. Please ensure the matrix notes the difference between list and committed overage prices and that the monthly vs quarterly true-up is clearly flagged as negotiable.

Marissa
VP, Commercials — Redwood Inference
Attachment: commercial-term-sheet-draft.pdf

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmehealth.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage tier carveouts and stepdown discount conditions

Avery, Marissa —

Appreciate the fast follow and the matrix. A couple of final clarifications before we share with legal and finance: 

• Can you confirm the explicit overage per-1k-token price for generation (post-commit) in $/1k-token? The matrix shows percentages but we need an explicit invoiceable line item for our modeler.

• Confirm embeddings overage mapping if the customer chooses not to include embeddings in the commit band (we saw $40 list / $28 committed in your note — please confirm the overage if embeddings are carved out entirely).

• We need a short MAP (Mutual Action Plan) with the following milestones: SOW sign, Provisioning start, Pilot go-live, Production go-live, Quarterly QBR. Can you post a 1-page MAP to the shared Drive link and confirm a draft by Monday?

We attached the RFP excerpt for your reference. If you can confirm the two line items (gen overage $/1k-token and embeddings carveout overage $/1k-embedding-unit) we can move to term-sheet markup. Also confirm you're keeping the quarterly true-up option in the term sheet.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Mon 08/16 9:00 PT to finalize the MAP and pricing lines.

Best,
Samantha
Attachment: Acme_RFP_section_C_pricing.pdf
